project.name: Tokenization Platform
project.purpose: Self-hosted, permissioned, closed-loop real-world-asset tokenization platform, real-estate first, settling in Iranian Rial on an internal ledger
project.regulatory_posture: asserts no compliance; jurisdiction rules are configuration marked REQUIRES LOCAL LEGAL VALIDATION

architecture.backend: NestJS 11 on Express, TypeScript strict + exactOptionalPropertyTypes + noUncheckedIndexedAccess
architecture.frontend: Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, zero UI dependencies, hand-rolled design system
architecture.chain: EVM (anvil devnet), ERC-3643 (T-REX) + ONCHAINID, ethers v6
architecture.multi_tenancy: tenant_id everywhere; AsyncLocalStorage TenantContext; Prisma Proxy that forbids findUnique/update/upsert/delete
architecture.auth: jose JWT in httpOnly cookie or Bearer (cookie wins); argon2; TOTP MFA opt-in for officers; deny-by-default RBAC

current_milestone.name: Chain writes off the hot path — step 1 of 4 done
current_milestone.state: Step 1 (record the mint per allocation and make it idempotent) is COMPLETE and CI-green at df5594e. MintAllocation + AllocationMintLog, backed by allocation_mints with a UNIQUE index on (offering_id, investor_id) — the index is the guarantee, proven by firing four simultaneous claims at real Postgres. Three states: unminted, minted, and unresolved (claimed but never confirmed), where unresolved REFUSES rather than guessing, because re-minting may double-issue and skipping leaves a paying holder with nothing. Steps 2 and 4 remain; step 3 is blocked on an owner decision.

previous_milestones.name: External portal — started with the one piece that needed no new decisions
previous_milestones.state: FR-RA-4 (a MUST requirement) is complete: an auditor can verify total supply vs registry (already existed) and now distributions vs bank records (built this slice), via the EXISTING auditor role and REPORTING_READ permission. Reading the code before building surfaced that a ledger entry carried no link to the distribution that caused it — fixed at the domain port, the Prisma column, and the adapter, with a round-trip test proving the fix (TypeScript alone did not catch the adapter silently ignoring the new parameter). The rest of 4.4 — external accounts for auditor/regulator/valuer, an /external portal shell, and what a valuer submits — is deliberately NOT started: it needs owner decisions the code cannot answer, listed below. Owner decisions received 2026-08-23: external parties reuse StaffUser with roles (no separate identity); Regulator deferred, matching the PRD's '(future)' marking; valuer submission stays staff-entered, so ATTESTATION_PUBLISH is unchanged and no external write path is built. With those answers, 4.4's remaining scope is the /external portal shell only. The /external portal shell was deliberately NOT built: with external parties reusing StaffUser, the permission-filtered admin nav already gives an auditor a read-only console, and a parallel portal would re-present the same screens. Verified by signing in as the auditor.

previous_milestones.name: Sanctions & PEP screening — a mock that cannot lie about itself
previous_milestones.state: Shipped and verified in a browser: an officer can screen an applicant and reads the outcome with a SIMULATED disclaimer beside it; an applicant with no declared name is refused with 409 and a readable reason. The adapter checks nothing and says so — simulated: true is hard-coded in the mock, and the disclaimer lives in the result, not in a log line. Results are append-only. Choosing a real provider remains an owner decision (OD-11). Risk rating now ships alongside it: an officer rates an applicant against a PROVISIONAL model (REQUIRES LOCAL LEGAL VALIDATION, shown on the card), the rating is advisory and decides nothing, and an unrated file reads as unrated rather than low. Periodic review scheduling — the third part of the roadmap's 4.2 line — is NOT built. Periodic review scheduling now completes the roadmap's 4.2 line: approved customers whose review has lapsed appear on their own screen, worst first, with never-reviewed ranked ahead of overdue. The cadence is provisional and shown as such. No scheduler runs and nothing is restricted — it is a work list.

4.2: which real sanctions/PEP provider (if any) should replace the mock? Until one is chosen the platform screens nobody, and every result is labelled SIMULATED in the officer's view.

3.3 exit criterion, still unmet: how much of the asset submission wizard should exist (drafts, completeness, validation, review comments, status history)? A scope call, not an engineering one — carried forward from the 3.3 milestone.

4.2 risk model: the factors and weights in `application/risk/risk-model.ts` are a generic placeholder I wrote, NOT a methodology. Which factors, which weights, and where the medium/high thresholds sit are compliance-policy inputs — replace them before any production use.

4.2 periodic review: how often must a customer be re-screened and re-rated (commonly risk-driven: e.g. high annually, low every few years)? The cadence is a policy input; the scheduling machinery is not built and is the remaining part of roadmap 4.2.
4.2 review cadence: high 12 / medium 24 / low 36 months is a placeholder shape (higher band reviewed more often), not a policy. Confirm or replace in `application/risk/risk-model.ts`.

4.2 periodic review: should a lapsed review DO anything beyond appearing on the list — a reminder to the officer, or a restriction on the customer? Today it does neither, deliberately; a restriction is a compliance-policy decision and a reminder needs an audience (the pg-boss scanner precedent used 'staff holding the permission').

4.2: should the periodic-review list join the ops work queue? Its contents (pending KYC + approvals + redemptions) were YOUR decision on 2026-07-28, so I built this as its own screen rather than widening that queue.
4.3: should a document decision need four eyes (a second reviewer), as payouts do? Today one officer accepting a document is enough to move an asset toward approval.
4.3: should the document review queue carry an SLA or ageing indicator? It currently shows what is outstanding but not how long it has waited.

4.3 Investor 360: an Audit tab needs a per-investor audit trail, which does not exist — `asset_events` is asset-scoped. Should privileged actions ON a person (KYC decisions, screenings, risk ratings, tag/stage changes) be recorded in a queryable per-subject trail? That is a schema addition, not a UI one.

4.3: should approving a KYC application be BLOCKED when the applicant has never been screened or risk-rated? Today the workspace warns at the moment of deciding but still allows it — a gate is a compliance-policy decision.
